stem.en: The liability of a sole proprietor is:

explanation.en: If business assets are not enough, the proprietor's personal assets can be used to pay business debts.

stem.en: Which of the following is a limitation of sole proprietorship?

explanation.en: One person cannot be an expert in every area of management; the other three are merits.

stem.en: 'A sole proprietorship has no separate legal entity' means that:

options.en: The business cannot own any property
The business must be registered with the government
In the eyes of law the owner and the business are one and the same

explanation.en: The law does not distinguish between the proprietor and the business; the owner is liable for all its activities.

stem.en: A sole trader's business debts are ₹5,00,000 and business assets are only ₹3,20,000. How much can creditors recover from his personal property?

explanation.en: Because liability is unlimited, the shortfall ₹5,00,000 − ₹3,20,000 = ₹1,80,000 can be recovered from personal assets.

stem.en: The eldest member who manages a Joint Hindu Family business is called the:

explanation.en: The business is controlled and managed by the eldest member of the family, called the Karta.

stem.en: Membership of a Joint Hindu Family business is acquired by:

explanation.en: A person becomes a member (coparcener) by birth in the family; no agreement is needed.

stem.en: The liability of the coparceners (other than the Karta) in a Joint Hindu Family business is:

options.en: Limited to their share in the coparcenary property

explanation.en: Only the Karta has unlimited liability; other members are liable only to the extent of their share in the family property.

stem.en: What happens to a Joint Hindu Family business on the death of the Karta?

options.en: The next eldest member becomes the Karta and the business continues

explanation.en: Its existence is not affected by the death of the Karta; the next eldest member takes over.

stem.en: Which statement about the Dayabhaga system of Hindu law is correct?

options.en: It prevails all over India except West Bengal and allows only males to be coparceners
It prevails in West Bengal and allows both male and female members to be coparceners
It prevails in Kerala and allows only female members to be coparceners
It allows only the Karta to be a coparcener

explanation.en: As per NCERT, Dayabhaga prevails in West Bengal and allows both male and female members to be coparceners; Mitakshara prevails in the rest of India.

stem.en: Partnership in India is governed by the Indian Partnership Act of:

explanation.en: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 defines and governs partnership.

stem.en: A partner who contributes capital and shares profits but does not take part in running the business is a:

explanation.en: A sleeping or dormant partner contributes capital and shares profits and losses but does not take part in day-to-day management.

stem.en: A partner who only lends his name to the firm, contributes no capital and takes no share of profit, but is liable to outsiders, is a:

explanation.en: A nominal partner lends his name and goodwill; he is liable to third parties for the firm's debts.

stem.en: The maximum number of partners in a partnership firm, as presently prescribed by the Central Government, is:

explanation.en: The Companies Act, 2013 allows up to 100; the Central Government has prescribed a maximum of 50 partners.

stem.en: Which of the following is a consequence of NOT registering a partnership firm?

options.en: The firm cannot file a suit against third parties
The firm becomes illegal and must close

explanation.en: Registration is optional, but an unregistered firm cannot sue third parties, and a partner cannot sue the firm or other partners.

stem.en: A, B and C are partners with capitals of ₹50,000, ₹30,000 and ₹20,000. There is no partnership deed. Profit for the year is ₹1,20,000. A's share of profit is:

explanation.en: In the absence of a deed, partners share profits equally: ₹1,20,000 ÷ 3 = ₹40,000 each, whatever their capitals.

stem.en: Sameer is a:

explanation.en: He contributes capital and shares profits but takes no part in management.

passage.en: Raghav and Sameer started a computer repair business in Mysuru without a written partnership deed. Raghav invested ₹1,00,000 and runs the shop every day. Sameer invested ₹2,00,000 but does not take part in running the business. Their friend Ali, a well-known engineer, allows the firm to show his name on its signboard to win customers' trust; he has invested nothing and takes no share in profits. The firm earned a profit of ₹60,000 this year.

stem.en: Ali is a nominal partner. Which statement about him is correct?

options.en: He shares the profit of ₹60,000 equally
He has no liability at all
He must manage the firm daily
He is liable to outsiders for the debts of the firm

explanation.en: A nominal partner lends his name, does not share profits, but is liable to third parties for the firm's debts.

passage.en: Raghav and Sameer started a computer repair business in Mysuru without a written partnership deed. Raghav invested ₹1,00,000 and runs the shop every day. Sameer invested ₹2,00,000 but does not take part in running the business. Their friend Ali, a well-known engineer, allows the firm to show his name on its signboard to win customers' trust; he has invested nothing and takes no share in profits. The firm earned a profit of ₹60,000 this year.

stem.en: With no deed, how will Raghav and Sameer share the profit of ₹60,000?

explanation.en: Without a deed, profits are shared equally between the partners: ₹60,000 ÷ 2 = ₹30,000. Ali is not entitled to profit.

passage.en: Raghav and Sameer started a computer repair business in Mysuru without a written partnership deed. Raghav invested ₹1,00,000 and runs the shop every day. Sameer invested ₹2,00,000 but does not take part in running the business. Their friend Ali, a well-known engineer, allows the firm to show his name on its signboard to win customers' trust; he has invested nothing and takes no share in profits. The firm earned a profit of ₹60,000 this year.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): A minor can be admitted to the benefits of a partnership firm.
Reason (R): A minor is competent to enter into a valid contract.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: With the consent of all partners a minor can be admitted to the benefits of the firm, but a minor cannot enter into a valid contract, so R is false.

stem.en: Voting in a cooperative society follows the principle of:

explanation.en: Every member has one vote irrespective of the number of shares held.

stem.en: The minimum number of members needed to form a cooperative society is:

explanation.en: At least ten members are required to form a cooperative society under the Cooperative Societies Act, 1912.

stem.en: Small farmers pool their produce and sell it together to get a better price. This is a:

explanation.en: Marketing cooperatives help small producers sell their output collectively and eliminate middlemen.

stem.en: A society that gives loans to members at easy terms and protects them from moneylenders is a:

explanation.en: Credit cooperatives provide financial help to members at reasonable rates of interest.

stem.en: The primary motive of a cooperative society is:

explanation.en: Cooperatives exist mainly to serve members, though they may earn a small surplus.

stem.en: The minimum number of members required to form a public company is:

explanation.en: A public company needs at least 7 members; a private company needs at least 2.

stem.en: The maximum number of members in a private company (excluding present and past employees) is:

explanation.en: The Companies Act, 2013 limits a private company to 200 members.

stem.en: 'Perpetual succession' of a company means that:

options.en: Its shares can never be transferred
Its directors hold office for life
It can never be wound up
Its existence is not affected by the death, insolvency or exit of its members

explanation.en: A company is created by law and can be ended only by law; members may come and go but the company continues.

stem.en: The liability of a shareholder in a company limited by shares is limited to:

options.en: The total assets of the company
The unpaid amount on the shares held

explanation.en: A shareholder's liability is limited to the amount, if any, still unpaid on his shares.

stem.en: Which statement about a private company is correct?

options.en: It must have at least 7 members
It cannot invite the public to subscribe to its securities
It has no upper limit on members

explanation.en: A private company restricts transfer of shares, limits members to 200 and prohibits invitation to the public; a public company needs 7 members.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Shareholders of a company are not personally liable for its debts beyond the unpaid amount on their shares.
Reason (R): A company is a separate legal entity distinct from its members.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Because the company is a separate legal person, its debts are its own; members lose at most the unpaid amount on their shares. R explains A.

stem.en: A business where direct personal contact with customers is essential, such as tailoring or a beauty parlour, is best run as a:

explanation.en: Personal attention and quick decisions make sole proprietorship suitable for such businesses.

stem.en: A business that needs very large capital and wants limited liability for its owners should choose:

explanation.en: A company can raise large capital from many shareholders and offers limited liability.

stem.en: Which form of organisation offers the greatest continuity of existence?

explanation.en: Because of perpetual succession, a company continues regardless of changes in membership.

stem.en: An owner who wants full control and complete secrecy of business information would prefer:

explanation.en: A sole proprietor need not share decisions or information with anyone.

stem.en:
Match List I (form of organisation) with List II (feature):
A. Sole proprietorship  B. Joint Hindu Family business  C. Cooperative society  D. Joint stock company
I. One member, one vote  II. Perpetual succession  III. Membership by birth  IV. Sole bearer of risk

explanation.en: The sole proprietor alone bears risk; JHF membership comes by birth; a cooperative gives one vote to each member; a company has perpetual succession.

stem.en:
Which of the following statements about a partnership firm are correct?
A. Registration of the firm is compulsory.
B. In the absence of a deed, profits are shared equally.
C. Every partner is an agent of the firm and of the other partners.
D. The liability of partners is limited to their capital.

explanation.en: Registration is optional and partners have unlimited liability, so A and D are wrong. B (equal sharing without a deed) and C (mutual agency) are correct.

stem.en: Promoters of a new steel plant need ₹500 crore from the general public, want the liability of investors to be limited and want the business to continue regardless of changes in ownership. The most suitable form of organisation is:

explanation.en: Only a public company can invite the general public to buy shares; it also offers limited liability and perpetual succession.
